problem: Social navigation robots typically cannot communicate their decision-making in human-readable, real-time form. Existing XAI in robotics stays with internal decision logic and lacks multimodal (vision + language) explanations.
motivation: Transparency lets users anticipate robot behavior and builds trust in human-robot interaction, especially around people in shared spaces. The authors combine captioning, saliency heatmaps and an LLM so a robot can explain what it sees and why it reroutes.
key_idea: A ROS2 explainability module chains BLIP captioning, Grad-CAM heatmap summaries and a GPT-3.5 prompt to produce spoken and displayed one-sentence explanations of navigation rerouting around social conflicts.
insight: Enabling explanations gave modest navigation gains (e.g. autonomous time 25.3 s to 22.6 s, sudden stops 21 to 18) and higher user-reported trust and understanding. Latency is the main obstacle (average about 20 s, up to 50.7 s on a Raspberry Pi with remote APIs). The evidence is small-scale and survey-based, with no ablation of individual components.
method: Camera Node: captures an image on request every ~5 s and publishes it to /camera/imageRaw.
BLIP Node: generates a contextual caption of the image using BLIP via the Hugging Face API, published on /blip/caption.
Heatmap Node: applies Grad-CAM with a ResNet to produce a saliency overlay and computes the percentage of the image attended to, published on /heatmap/summary.

LLM Node: GPT-3.5 Turbo through the Azure OpenAI API merges caption and heatmap summary using a guiding prompt (one sentence, starts with 'I see', ends with a rerouting phrase), then outputs speech and a display overlay.

Problem formulation: navigation task tuple with social norm constraints (safe and social distance, acceleration limit, group-respect function h) and a survey-derived explainability factor epsilon in [0,1].
Evaluation: manual vs autonomous navigation, with and without explanations, on a MYAGV robot; a 30-person user survey; confusion-matrix check against human labels.

setting.backbone: BLIP (pretrained, via Hugging Face API) + ResNet Grad-CAM + GPT-3.5 Turbo (frozen, Azure OpenAI)
setting.training_data: none (uses pretrained models off the shelf)
setting.observation: monocular RGB from the onboard camera
setting.action_space: standard ROS navigation stack (autonomous or manual driving); explanations do not directly control actions

numbers_note: No standard embodied-navigation benchmark; results are custom real-robot metrics (trajectory 5.76 m, time 23.5 s vs 22.1 s manual; 25.3 s vs 22.6 s autonomous), a user survey (n=30, preference score 76.7%) and a confusion matrix (196 images, TP 82, FN 15, FP 20, TN 79, accuracy 82.14%).
results: With explanations, autonomous time fell from 25.3 s to 22.6 s and sudden stops from 21 to 18; 76.7% preference, +16.7% trust and +23.3% understanding in the user survey. The explanation accuracy against human labels is 82.14% on 196 images. There is no strong baseline; the comparison is with and without the module.
limitations: Explanation latency averages about 20 s (5.986 to 50.688 s) on a Raspberry Pi with cloud LLM/VLM calls, too slow for true real-time.
Small-scale evaluation (n=30 survey, 4 runs, short hallway tests) with subjective metrics and no ablations or comparison to other explanation methods.
Explanations are post-hoc descriptions from caption and heatmap; the Grad-CAM heatmap is on a ResNet, not the actual navigation policy, so faithfulness to the real decision is unverified.
builds_on: Explainable robotic vehicles framework (Shekar et al. 2024)
